impact_bands.label: Miss
impact_bands.fight: The GM makes a move against you
impact_bands.outside: It fails or goes wrong, GM makes a move

impact_bands.label: Impact 1
impact_bands.outside: You get it, with a cost or complication

impact_bands.label: Impact 3
impact_bands.outside: Success plus a bonus (a clue, a position, an opening)

stats.name: Force
stats.act: Hit hard, break things, lift, hold on

stats.name: Focus
stats.act: Investigate, hack, use gadgets, read people

toughness.text: Force +3 or higher gives Toughness 1. Toughness reduces the Harm of each hit by 1, after weapon bonuses, but a hit always does at least 1 Harm. The roll's Impact is unchanged. It doesn't work against guns unless you have armor or a power that says it does. Toughness doesn't stack: use your single highest source for that attack. Only effects that say "+1 Toughness" add on top. Toughness can never go above 2. Gas, fire, electricity, and other hazards ignore it unless a power or piece of armor says otherwise.

attack_kinds.name: Guns
attack_kinds.text: Bullets. Toughness only from armor or a power that says so

attack_kinds.name: Hazards
attack_kinds.text: Gas, fire, electricity. Ignores Toughness unless something says otherwise

box_text.Bruised: No effect. Clears after any short breather.
box_text.Hurt: No effect yet, but you're one box from real trouble.
box_text.Battered: No effect. An extra box from Hard to Kill or the Resilience power.
box_text.Wounded: Disadvantage on Force and Flow rolls. Grit your teeth: at the start of your turn, take 1 Stress to ignore it until your next turn.
box_text.Down: Out of the fight. Talk, crawl, or one desperate Quick Action per round at Disadvantage. Or spend your whole turn on Second Wind (3 Drive, no roll, once per fight).

harm.dying_text: If a Downed hero takes more Harm, they're Dying. A single hit stops at Down. An ally can spend a Full Action next to them to stabilize them. Death is decided at the table: if a Dying hero isn't stabilized by the end of the scene, their player decides. Either the hero's story ends here, or they are left for dead: they survive, stay Down until Dawn, and tick their Home clock twice, because you're too fucked up to manage your life at all.

grit_your_teeth.text: At the start of your turn, a Wounded hero can take 1 Stress to ignore the Wounded Disadvantage until their next turn.

harm.bruiser_text: Bruisers (trial). Some mooks are tougher: enforcers, bouncers, riot cops. A bruiser has 2 Harm boxes and no Toughness. Bruisers take Harm the way a named enemy does, so weapon bonuses count. Every 2 Harm drops one, and Harm left over carries to the next bruiser in the group. An Impact 3 doesn't drop a second bruiser by itself: its Harm drops one and staggers the next. Anything that takes a mook out with no Harm (a tranquilizer dart, a taser gun) deals 1 Harm to a bruiser instead. In every other way they are mooks: they act as a group, their attacks cap at 2 Harm, and they lose turns as written.

weapons.name: Light melee
weapons.text: +1 Harm on a Strike at Impact 2 or better. Jabs with it have no -2 penalty.

weapons.name: Heavy melee
weapons.text: +1 Harm on any hit, but only on a Strike (never a Jab)

weapons.name: Blades
weapons.text: +1 Harm on Impact 2 or better against anyone with no Toughness

weapons.name: Guns
weapons.text: +1 Harm on Impact 2 or better and ignores Toughness. Firing one is loud: +1 Heat

stages.name: Steady
stages.text: Your Trait's Steady perk is on.

stages.name: Fraying
stages.text: Your Trait's Fraying perk replaces the Steady perk. The GM gets your Trait's hook.

stages.name: Breaking
stages.text: Your Trait's Breaking fallout takes over for the rest of the scene.

stress.villain_breaking_text: A Breaking villain does not leave the fight. Their Breaking line takes over for the rest of the scene, and every attack against them has Edge. If the line says they flee, the heroes get one round to stop them.

earn.source: Going along with the GM's hook while Fraying
Breaking (at the end of the scene)

prices.name: Edge
prices.text: +2 to a roll. Before you roll.

prices.name: Upgrade
prices.text: Raise a hit by one Impact level (1 to 2, or 2 to 3). After any roll that hits, once per roll.

prices.name: Signature Move
prices.text: On your turn, as its own action.

prices.name: Second Wind
prices.text: Once per fight, no roll: clear one Harm box as a Full Action. For a Downed hero it takes the whole turn and puts them back up at Wounded.

strain.text: Once per turn, take 1 Stress to get an extra Quick Action.

push.text: When your power helps a roll, take 1 Stress to roll with Advantage.

slots.text: Every hero gets 3 slots: gear and street powers cost 1, a strange power costs 2 and needs a flaw. At creation, at most one strange power. Specialists and Gadgeteers also get a utility belt, which sits on top of their slots.

full.name: Strike
full.text: Attack with Force, Flow, or Presence. Normal Impact. A heavy melee attack is a Strike.

full.name: Stabilize
full.text: Save a Dying ally next to you.

quick.name: Jab
quick.text: A quick attack at -2 (no penalty with light melee). A hit is always Impact 1, so bonuses that need Impact 2 or better never apply. Once per turn.

quick.name: Help
quick.text: Give an ally in your zone Edge on their next roll.

quick.name: Take Cover
quick.text: In a Cover zone, +2 Guard until your next turn.

quick.name: Interact
quick.text: Grab, open, throw a switch, kick a gun away.

actions.free_move: One free move: to an adjacent zone (you can also engage one enemy there), or into or out of engagement in your zone.
actions.breaking_away: If you leave engagement, the enemy you were engaged with can make a free Jab at you.
actions.chases: When someone runs and someone follows, each round the chasers pick one hero to roll Flow against the quarry's Guard (a car or a rooftop route uses a rating instead). Three hits catch them, and an Impact 3 counts as two. Three Misses and they're gone. When the heroes are the ones running, they roll the same way against the pursuers' Wits: three hits and they're clear.
actions.leaving_fight: From a zone with an exit, when you aren't engaged, spend your turn to leave. If you're engaged, break away first as usual, then spend your turn. Rooftop Runner skips the turn cost.
actions.hidden_ends: Hidden ends when you attack, when you leave the zone tags that allow it (or they go away), or when an enemy spends a Quick Action to search and beats your Flow-based roll: they roll Focus against 12 + your Flow. Mooks search with their attack bonus.

clocks.name: Scheme
clocks.ticks: Every Dawn, and as a cost when following leads
clocks.half: Beats at 2, 4 and 6: three events the heroes can see, written in case prep (a witness disappears, a building burns)
clocks.full: The villain pulls it off. The showdown happens on their ground, after the damage is done.

clocks.name: Heat
clocks.ticks: Guns, public fights, collateral damage, Vanity, Vengeance, sloppy feeding, a Marked hero seen by civilians
clocks.half: Cops show up to fights on round 3 and try to arrest everyone, heroes included
clocks.full: Crackdown: a task force, a smear in the press, or someone gets a description. Play it out, then drop Heat to 2.

clocks.name: Home
clocks.ticks: You skip Show Up, you Break, you use a personal clue, you use Resources to buy past a problem, or a villain finds your Lair (+2)
clocks.full: Home crisis: lose the job, the relationship ends, someone learns who you are, or a loved one becomes a target. Play it out, then reset to 0.

clocks.name: Endgame
clocks.ticks: A case's Scheme clock fills (+2); a Pawn escapes or a theory names the wrong culprit (+1); the heroes miss an Unmasking roll (+1)
clocks.half: The Mastermind makes it personal: pick one hero and hit their Home
clocks.full: The Endgame happens. The finale becomes damage control instead of prevention.

complexity.text: 4 for a one-Night job. A normal case is 2 plus twice the number of heroes: 6 for two heroes (or one), 8 for three, 10 for four. An arc finale is 2 more than a normal case.

lead_results.text: The clue, and the GM picks a cost: tick the Scheme clock, +1 Heat, 1 Stress, or an ambush
The clue, and you pick one of those costs
The clue, plus one: a second clue, Edge against the villain in the showdown, or a hint at their Weakness

crack_results.text: Wrong. The GM says which facet doesn't hold up. The team picks one: Regroup (the Scheme clock ticks twice; try again once you have at least one new clue) or Go in anyway (the Scheme clock ticks once, and you walk into a trap).
Right, with a snag: they're ready for you, or it's the right place but the wrong night
Right, and you also learn the villain's Weakness or gain an arc clue

missed_crack.trap_text: Going in on a wrong theory is a Confrontation on the villain's ground, and their side ambushes. The case villain isn't there unless the Scheme clock is full: the trap is a lieutenant or a gang. Wrong Who: you corner a patsy as a clean-up crew arrives (the Objective is keeping the patsy alive). Wrong What: you walk into a live job (+1 Heat, cops on round 2). Wrong Where: a decoy (one zone is a Hazard, and a clock of 4 counts down). Win the fight or finish its Objective and the team takes 1 clue, and the GM gives the true answer to the facet that was wrong.

confrontation.text: You choose the ground. Ambush the villain (your side has Edge on its first roll), or add one zone tag of your choice to the map.
You know where, but they're ready. No ambush either way, and the villain starts with +1 Drive.
A trap, or a full Scheme clock: the villain chooses the ground and gets the ambush.

dawn.order: At the start of Dawn, the Scheme clock ticks and its Stress lands, before heroes make their picks.

options.name: Patch Up
options.text: Clear Hurt and Wounded. Pick both this and Sleep It Off to clear Down.

options.name: Show Up
options.text: Be there for your civilian life. Play a short scene with one of your connections, then clear 1 Stress. If you don't pick this, tick your Home clock.

options.name: Work the Case
options.text: Chase one lead off-screen and take 1 clue, no roll.

patrol.text: Each hero gets 2 Patrol actions per Night. Following a lead costs one. A hero can take at most one no-roll clue per Night, from all sources combined (Work the Case, Plugs, Network, forensic kit, hacking rig, tracker and the like).

defeat.text: When every hero is Down or has fled, the villain gets what they came for, the Scheme clock ticks twice, and each hero ticks Home or Heat (their choice). Nobody dies from defeat alone: a Dying hero is stabilized by a bystander, or because the villain walks away.

recovery.name: Breather
recovery.text: A few quiet minutes between scenes: clear Bruised.

recovery.name: Dawn
recovery.text: Patch Up clears Hurt and Wounded.

recovery.name: Down after a fight
recovery.text: A hero who is Down (but not Dying) gets back up at Wounded when the fight ends, at Disadvantage on Force and Flow until they heal. A stabilized Dying hero stays Down until Dawn and needs Patch Up and Sleep It Off together.

stress_sources.text: You Strain for an extra action
Someone you're protecting gets hurt or dies on your watch
The GM makes a hard move against you (on top of what the move costs)
The Scheme clock ticks (the hero whose roll caused it; everyone at Dawn or on a missed Crack)
You see an ally go Down (first time each fight)

villain_scaling.lieutenant_text: A lieutenant gets one turn per round, however many heroes there are. With several named enemies, each villain takes its own turns and no villain counts as alone.
villain_scaling.turns_text: A named villain gets one turn per round for every two heroes, rounded up. A villain fighting alone, with no mooks or lieutenants, gets one turn per hero instead.
villain_scaling.gang_text: With no named villain, one group of 3 mooks per hero. With a named villain present, one group per two heroes (rounded down, minimum 1). Then adjust for how hard the fight should be.
villain_scaling.named_enemy_text: A named enemy can lose at most one turn per fight, from all sources combined. After that, any effect that would cost them a turn gives them Disadvantage on their next roll instead. Losing their next Quick Action means Disadvantage on their next roll.

advancement: +1 to a stat (max +4, and never two cases in a row)
The next ability on one of your powers
A new slot (gear or a street power; a strange power needs two slots, so it takes two picks)
